hip_flex.source: ACE Romanian Deadlift: push the hips back and lower the weight until tension is felt along the hamstrings, bar tracking to about the mid-shin; no exact angle is given, so 75 degrees is an illustrative end for that depth (thin source, flagged for an owner device check)

knee_flex.source: ThatFitFriend RDL technique: keep a slight, fixed knee bend of about 10 to 20 degrees for the whole rep

torso_lean.source: ACE Romanian Deadlift: keep a straight back; the trunk stays rigid on the pelvis through the hip hinge (the lean itself comes from hip_flex, not the spine)

muscles.peakSource: EMG comparison of conventional and Romanian deadlifts (ScienceDirect S1728869X18301291): hamstring activation is highest at the stretched bottom position, just before the concentric drive back up

mistake.name: Squat it up

tells.text: The knees bend forward like a squat instead of holding their angle.
The hips barely go back, so the bar drifts out in front of the legs.

mistake.source: ThatFitFriend (5 RDL Mistakes and Fixes) and SimpliFaster: bending the knees turns the hinge into a squat and shifts load off the hamstrings; hips not going back far enough is the same fault seen as the bar drifting away from the body, which loads the lower back instead

sources: Contact fact (bar over mid-foot / kept against the legs): ACE Romanian Deadlift — "keep the bar against the body the entire time; the farther the bar hovers away from the body, the greater the stress on the lower back"
